front: When did Britain abolish its slave trade?
When did Britain's Slavery Abolition Act come into force?

back: Trade in goods such as palm oil, groundnuts and ivory, which Europeans hoped would replace the trade in people.
A formerly enslaved African whose autobiography (1789) helped the abolition campaign.

front: Who led the abolition campaign in the British Parliament?
back: William Wilberforce, an evangelical Christian MP.

front: What did Eric Williams argue about abolition?
back: In Capitalism and Slavery (1944) he argued abolition came mainly because slavery became less profitable to industrial Britain; others stress humanitarian and religious campaigns.

front: Give four negative effects of the slave trade on Africa.
back: Depopulation; insecurity and wars; decline of crafts; decline of farming (also brutalisation and, some argue, long-term underdevelopment).

front: Why was the slave trade hard to end?
back: Continuing demand in Brazil and Cuba; a long coast to patrol; other nations' ships; African rulers' interests; the growing East African trade.
